Subject: Pilot -> paid: term timing and termination mechanics

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move our pilot into a paid billing arrangement we need to align on a few contract mechanics so our procurement and legal teams can sign off:

- Pilot term length (we're thinking 90 days) and how that maps onto the Order Form term if we convert to paid.
- Auto-renew: what notice window triggers preventing automatic renewal?
- Termination for convenience (TFC): are there any fees or notice minimums if either party elects to exit during or after the pilot?
- Precedence: does the Order Form override MSA wording for term/renewal, or do you use MSA-first language?

I've attached our initial redlines to the Order Form to capture our preference (we prefer a 45-day notice to avoid auto-renew and a pilot carve-out permitting termination without penalty during the pilot). Can you confirm Redwood's standard position and, if possible, share suggested language so we can circulate internally?

Also happy to set a quick call this week to run through a mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Ethan
Ethan Walters
Director, Platform Integrations
BrightHealth

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot -> paid: term timing and termination mechanics

Ethan —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers and a couple of options below; I'll loop in Legal and Sales for the precise redlines.

1) Pilot term: agreeing a 90-day pilot works. We normally include a "Pilot Period" definition in the Order Form that supersedes the standard Term clause for that specific Order Form.

2) Auto-renew: our default hosted Order Forms auto-renew for successive 12‑month terms unless either party provides written notice prior to the end of the then-current term. Typical windows we offer are 60 days, but we're flexible — 45 days is often acceptable for pilots converting to paid.

3) Termination for convenience: post-conversion (paid term) we normally require 60 days' notice for TFC and no early-exit fee beyond any prepaid credit adjustments. For pilots we can add a carve-out: either party may terminate during the Pilot Period with 30 days' written notice and no penalty.

4) Precedence: Order Form controls commercial term length/renewal mechanics; MSA provides the overarching contract framework. We'll propose a short precedence sentence so there's no ambiguity.

Next steps I propose: (a) Legal produces a clean redline with explicit Pilot carve-out language and proposed Notice windows, (b) Sales confirms commercial concession if you want a shorter notice in exchange for a term commitment after pilot. I've attached our current MSA mark-up and will ask Legal to draft suggested Order Form language.

If this sounds good I'll ask Karthik to send the suggested text by EOD Monday. Also happy to jump on a 20-min call if you prefer.

Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Ethan / team —

Thanks for the context. I've drafted suggested redline language below for the Order Form and MSA interplay; putting the core bits inline to speed review. I've also attached a marked PDF of the MSA with where we'd prefer changes.

Suggested Order Form inserts (sample language):

"Pilot Period" means the period beginning on the Effective Date of this Order Form and continuing for ninety (90) days, unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Order Form. During the Pilot Period, either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party, without penalty.

"Renewal; Notice" Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the MSA, this Order Form shall, following the Pilot Period, have an initial term of twelve (12) months (the "Initial Term"). Except as otherwise provided in the Order Form, the Initial Term and each renewal term shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party gives the other written notice of non‑renewal at least forty‑five (45) days prior to the end of the then‑current term.

"Precedence" In the event of any inconsistency between the MSA and this Order Form with respect to Term, Renewal, or Termination for Convenience, the terms of this Order Form shall control.

Notes from Legal:
- We prefer the 45‑day window in your case (pilot-to-paid) — it balances operations and procurement timelines.
- Preserve a 60‑day TFC notice for multi-year committed deals; the 45‑day language above applies to the Order Form only.
- Add a short 'Order Form controls' precedence clause to avoid MSA/Order Form conflicts.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3_marked.pdf (full redline). I'll generate a DocuSign-ready Order Form after you confirm the 45/30 split.

Karthik Iyer
Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
